title: Routebook -> Microtask transpiler for cost-aware admin flows
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Problem: long, free-form runbooks are hard to execute reliably in emergency or low-trust contexts. They lead to manual drift, unpredictable operator time, and inconsistent token/cost profiles when run with automated helpers.

Goal: build a lightweight 'routebook' transpiler that converts existing runbooks into an ordered set of idempotent microtasks (tasklets) enriched with telemetry hooks and cost estimates. Tasklets must be safe to run interactively by oncall, programmatically by the Ops Assistant, or scheduled for unattended remediation.

Outcomes:
- Canonical microtask format (YAML+metadata) with explicit inputs, outputs, preconditions, and rollback hints.
- Static cost model that estimates token + infra cost per tasklet.
- Runtime instrumentation: operator time, success/failure, token consumption, and cost delta emitted to Console telemetry.
- Exporters to the Admin Playbook catalog and the quickpatch kiosk.

Non-goals: implementing automated remediation policies (that will be a follow-up), re-authoring runbooks manually (we'll support automated and minimal human review flows).
acceptance_criteria: Transpiler prototype converts 90% of canonical runbook steps to tasklets with defined inputs/outputs
Each generated tasklet includes a static token+infra cost estimate (within +/-40% of measured in canary)
Console shows telemetry: execution duration, operator id, token usage, and cost for each tasklet in a sample rollout
Generated tasklets are idempotent (documented by preconditions/rollback hints) and pass a safety linter
Exported artifacts appear in the Admin Playbook catalog under a new 'routebook' namespace
implementation_notes: Phase 1: parser + rule-based step splitter (handle shell steps, query steps, manual check steps)
Phase 2: cost estimator that maps step types to token and GPU-second heuristics (pluggable model profiles)
Phase 3: telemetry hooks and Console integration (traces + per-tasklet cost breakdown)
Phase 4: CLI 'rbx generate' to create tasklet bundles and a dry-run validator
Safety: embed a liveness gate and 'require-approval' flag for any tasklet that changes production state
steps: Inventory top 150 runbooks and identify common step patterns (shell, api-call, human-check, model-infer)
Design tasklet schema and linter rules (PR: #821-rb/tasklet-spec)
Implement parser for Markdown and legacy runbook DSL to canonical step IR
Add cost mapping table and implement simple estimator function
Render tasklets to YAML and wire Console import endpoint
Run 10 pilot runbooks with oncall to validate interactive UX and telemetry
progress_updates: 2026-02-25: Kickoff sync with PM and Design. Agreed on non-goals and success metrics. -- Diego
2026-02-28: PoC parser can split example runbooks into 3 step categories. Found ~12% of steps are ambiguous (requires manual review). -- Aisha
2026-03-04: Cost estimator prototype (rule table) implemented. Mapped common model infer steps to token heuristics. Initial variance high for third-party API calls.
2026-03-09: Design provided microtask UI mockups and suggested 'approve-and-run' flow for high-risk tasklets (link below). -- Sofia Alvarez

2026-03-12: First end-to-end transpile of a production runbook produced 14 tasklets; imported to playbook catalog successfully. Console telemetry shows token and duration metrics in Grafana panel. -- Diego
2026-03-14: Safety linter added with rules for idempotency and 'no-implicit-destroys'. Flagged 2 tasklets that require 'require-approval'. Preparing pilot run with SRE. -- Aisha
decisions: Prefer rule-based transpilation + human-in-the-loop review over ML-based translation for initial MVP (faster, auditable)
Represent cost as two numbers: estimated_token_units and infra_seconds to separate model vs infra costs
Tasklets default to 'require-approval' if they target production clusters or mutate state for more than 2 minutes
risks_mitigations: Risk: Overtrust in static cost estimates. Mitigation: show confidence bands and require early telemetry comparisons for calibration
Risk: Non-idempotent legacy steps. Mitigation: safety linter that forces manual remediation or wrap in transactional guard
Risk: Catalog sprawl. Mitigation: add metadata tags and 'last-reviewed' timestamp; periodic housekeeping job planned
notes_for_reviewers: Focus on the tasklet schema and safety linter rules in the first pass
Telemetry contract: we need a minimal set of fields (tasklet_id, operator, duration_ms, token_units, infra_seconds, success)
Please triage any step types that are common in your oncall runbooks and add examples to the shared spreadsheet
